ModelSelection.description: One exact base or named-variant model selection.

PermissionEffect.description:
A value this build does not know reads as `ask`: asking, the effect that
never runs a call unapproved.

PermissionMode.description: A value this build does not know reads as `ask`: asking.

action.description: Permission action a tool declares, such as `read`, `bash`, or a runtime's own action.

resource.description: Current wildcard grammar: '*' matches any characters, '?' matches one character, and the exact '${workspace_dir}' expression is allowed; controls, globstar, escapes, classes, and every other brace form are forbidden. Runtime deserialization additionally enforces a maximum of 4096 UTF-8 bytes; x-cookie-agent-maxUtf8Bytes records that byte limit because JSON Schema maxLength counts Unicode code points.

runtime.description:
Runtime selector (`bash@labpc`): the rule applies only to tools of
runtimes with this runtime ID. Absent, it applies everywhere,
including the base layer.

ProducerDeliveryMode.description:
Per-send mode. Queue remains accepted-but-deferred during an active run;
steer joins the next safe request without interrupting an in-flight request.

ProjectRuntime.description:
One runtime a project's new sessions attach, as `session.create`'s
`runtimes` names it.

capability.description:
The capability to attach; the runtime's only capability when
omitted.

workspace.description: Required exactly when the capability takes a workspace.

WebhookCondition.description:
One condition of a webhook's filter: the value its source reads must be
one of `one_of`.

WebhookSignatureEncoding.description: How a generic HMAC signature is written.

oneOf.description:
A new root session per event, or per thread key, from this
template.

WebhookTemplate.description:
What a new-session webhook's sessions start with: a cron template's
members, with a thread key read from each request.

acp_runtime.description: For an ACP agent, the runtime its runs run it on.

agent.description:
The agent each session starts with; it must be able to run as a
root (`primary` or `all`).

global.description: Whether a session attaches the global runtime; `true` when omitted.

model.description:
A model pin; the agent's own model chain when omitted. Only clients
set it.

permission_rules.description: Rules added to each session as its permission overlay.

project.description: The project the sessions belong to.

runtimes.description:
The runtimes a session attaches besides `global`, as
`session.create`'s `runtimes` names them.

thread_key.description:
Where each request's thread key is read (section 7.4): events with
the same key go into one session, which the first of them creates.
Each event creates a session when omitted, and so does an event
whose key is missing.

thread_prompt.description:
Instructions each session the webhook creates gets once, as a plain
user message before its first event, and again before the first
event after each compaction of that session (section 7.5).

title.description:
What the sessions it creates are called (client protocol 1.97.0;
`docs/site/specs/webhooks-view.md` section 6): plain text, given when
the webhook is made, in place of its name in their titles, which the
thread key or the time still follows. Its name when omitted.

title_auto.description:
Whether each session it creates is left untitled for the automatic
title to name after its first turn, as a session the user starts is
(client protocol 1.97.0); `title` then goes unused. Off when
`[session_title] generate_on_first_turn` is.

WebhookValueSource.description:
Where a filter condition or a thread key reads its value: exactly one of
a request header, by name, or a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into a JSON or
form body.

WebhookVerify.description:
A webhook's check as commands set it and reads show it. `secret` is
the secret, or the bearer token, on a create or an update; the daemon
makes one when it is omitted and never returns it here (see
`webhooks.secret`). `header`, `encoding`, and `prefix` belong to
`hmac_sha256` only.

oneOf.description:
Standard Webhooks: `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and
`webhook-signature`, with a `whsec_` secret.
A bearer token in the `Authorization` header.

description:
Change a webhook. Only the members present change; `null` clears an
optional one. A `verify` of another kind, or with a `secret`, replaces
the secret; one of the same kind without a secret keeps it. Enabling the
webhook resets its failure count.

id.description: A webhook's ID: eight lowercase ASCII letters and digits.

title: WebhookUpdateParams
